children.title: O1 · Scope: no identifying mark
children.labelText: S · The dispute concerns ordinary lost objects without an identifying mark.

children.title: O2 · Marked objects: agreement
children.labelText: S · Both reject unconscious yeush here; later despair does not repair an already prohibited pickup.

children.title: O3 · Sea / river exception
children.labelText: S · The Torah permits the exceptional sea or river loss, even with a mark.

children.title: O4 · Abaye: no awareness
children.labelText: S · The owner has not yet learned of the loss.

children.title: O5 · Abaye: ineffective
children.labelText: S · Unconscious yeush is not effective in the disputed case.

children.title: O7 · Rava: effective now
children.labelText: S · In the disputed case, that anticipated despair counts now.

children.title: O6 · Rava: future despair
children.labelText: S · Once aware, the owner will despair because there is no identifying mark.

children.title: C1 · Scattered coins: permitted
children.labelText: S · The cited Mishnah lets the finder keep scattered coins.

children.title: C2 · Objection: owner unaware
children.labelText: S · The objection assumes that the owner has not learned of this loss.

children.title: C3 · Bridge: test Abaye
children.labelText: R · If permission holds while awareness is absent, this case conflicts with Abaye.

children.title: C5 · Reply: purse checking
children.labelText: S · People habitually check their purses, says Rabbi Yitzhak.

children.title: C6 · Owner already knew
children.labelText: E · The reply treats the owner as aware and despairing before the finder picked up the coins.

children.title: C7 · Coins do not decide
children.labelText: R · With unawareness denied, the coins case does not establish Rava over Abaye.

children.title: C4 · Coins challenge
children.labelText: R · Permission plus assumed unawareness challenges Abaye, using the stated bridge.

children.title: R1 · Verse: loss from you
children.labelText: S · Deuteronomy 22:3 is read as addressing loss from the owner that remains accessible to others.

children.title: R2 · Inaccessible loss: permitted
children.labelText: S · A river loss inaccessible to everyone is excluded from that obligation.

children.labelText: S · The Gemara compares prohibition and permission: each covers items with or without a mark.

children.labelText: E · For the ordinary-loss prohibition, the owner has not learned of the loss before pickup.
